question: On 9 November 2026, the Commission and the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) signed a new cooperation arrangement1,2 setting shared objectives and areas of cooperation. While recognising UEFA as football’s sole European governing body (Article 2.3) and requiring compliance with EU law (Article 1.5), the arrangement raises concerns about the safeguards accompanying this recognition.

It provides no explicit guarantees for the Commission’s independent enforcement role under EU competition law. Similarly, Article 3.2.8 promotes supporters’ participation without concrete commitments on ticket affordability, dynamic pricing or transparency. Furthermore, Article 7.
5 confirms that the arrangement creates no legally binding obligations, while Section 6 provides for dialogue without measurable targets, public reporting or independent evaluation. 1.
How will the Commission safeguard its independence in enforcing EU competition law and other applicable EU legislation in its dealings with UEFA?
How will it ensure tangible improvements for supporters, particularly regarding ticket affordability, pricing transparency and unfair dynamic pricing practices?
Will the Commission introduce measurable targets, regular public reporting and independent evaluations to ensure accountability and enable appropriate parliamentary scrutiny of the arrangement?
